tasks.short: Book the invoices and credit notes in AFAS

today.trigger: Supplier invoices, customer credit notes and bank files arrive by mail, as UBL, or through a staffing-agency portal.
steps: Open the document from Outlook or the AFAS inbox and find the supplier or debtor.
Check the amount, VAT, site and whether a purchase order or a goods receipt exists.
Type the lines and post, or park the document when a code or a receipt is missing.
Store the PDF on the creditor or debtor in AFAS.
Look the same figures up again when a site or FP&A asks.
drudgery: Retyping header and line amounts that a UBL file already contains.
Searching the mailbox for the PDF that belongs to a posting.
Rebuilding a supplier's recent invoices in Excel to see how they were booked last time.
today.time_sinks: Most of the hour goes to opening, typing and filing documents whose figures are already on the file.

lenses.faster: Posting and filing drop away for a UBL invoice that matches one order or one receipt. What stays is the PDF and the unmatched line, about a third of the time this task takes now, because each exception still has to be read.
lenses.autonomous: A UBL invoice or a CAMT.053 file landing in AFAS starts the posting. Exact one-to-one matches post on their own, and the bookkeeper receives only lines with no supplier, no receipt, or a VAT gap.
lenses.ambitious: Give the Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo site managers a same-week split of flex-agency cost, which they now see only as one lump in the nightly Power BI extract. Demand would grow if that split were cheap, because flex headcount moves between 150 and 300 with the season and each site already asks where its share went.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss retyping lines and dragging PDFs onto the right creditor. The work people want more of is a supplier that billed the wrong site, or a load that was never receipted.
lenses.options: Two posting drafts for an intra-EU carrier invoice, one with Dutch VAT and one with reverse charge, change whether the cost is booked or sent back to the supplier. A single suggested posting hides that choice.
lenses.altitude: The week becomes a short exception list and repairs to supplier and order data so the next invoice matches. They gain the right to set the amount tolerance and to send a bad file back before it is posted, and the job becomes more expert because the remaining documents are the awkward ones.
reach: The Accountant's first tie-out of the creditors and debtors sub-ledgers to the general ledger for the three sites, once they learn the close checklist and which differences the Controller still wants in the file.
The FP&A analyst's pull of posted warehouse cost by site for the weekly forecast, once they learn which accruals FP&A adds on top of the ledger.

tasks.human_edge: The bookkeeper can see when a match is numerically right and operationally wrong: a Venlo receipt used for a Rotterdam load, a credit note netted against the wrong shipment, or a supplier that changed legal entity and kept the same IBAN.
tasks.pattern_why: A one-to-one match of a UBL invoice to an order or a receipt is a rule AFAS already runs, and the posting follows from that match. Reading a messy PDF is a later step, used only when no UBL arrived.

in_practice.trigger: A UBL invoice, a PDF, or a CAMT.053 bank file arrives in AFAS.
steps: AFAS matches UBL lines to the purchase order or the goods receipt and posts the one-to-one hits.
A PDF without UBL is read into an e-invoice and the supplier is proposed from KvK number, VAT number and IBAN.
Lines with no match, no supplier or a VAT gap stay on a queue.
The bookkeeper completes or returns only that queue.
Posted items leave with the nightly extract to Power BI.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper releases or corrects every line that failed the match or that lacks a supplier, a VAT code or a site.
data_needed: Supplier KvK number, VAT number and IBAN
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS posting journal, with the match key and the user who cleared each exception.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 reads UBL and PDF invoices to line level, and a one-to-one match with an order or a receipt is posted and approved for payment.
A PDF without UBL is scanned into an e-invoice, the supplier is found from KvK number, VAT number and IBAN, and the remaining gaps are filled by hand.
Escalante Golf cut invoice handling from 2.5 minutes to 45 seconds. Coding is suggested for a person to review and confirm, and the same account says routine invoices process themselves.
A booking proposal is not the same as touchless posting. Own ledger accounts, VAT codes and exceptions keep people in the process, and PDFs and receipts keep arriving.

risks: A one-to-one amount match can still post a Rotterdam load against a Venlo receipt.
Scan and recognition can attach the wrong supplier where two legal entities share a VAT number or an IBAN.

The cabinet has chosen business e-invoicing from 1 July 2030 and reporting from 1 July 2031. A posting path that sits for two weeks in someone's mail will be late for that timetable once it is in force.
Agency invoices name flex workers. Copying those names into the ledger narrative spreads personal data further than the invoice file requires.
research_questions: What share of invoices arrived as UBL in the last three months, by supplier group?
What share of UBL invoices finds exactly one open order or receipt in AFAS today?
How many scan-and-recognition proposals does a bookkeeper change before posting, counted over four weeks?
Which ledger accounts and VAT codes differ by site or by administration?

tasks.short: Check the figures, VAT and codes on what was booked

today.trigger: A document has just been posted, or a supplier statement or debtor list is being checked.
steps: Recalculate line totals, VAT and the invoice total.
Compare the ledger account and VAT code with the supplier's usual coding and with the site.
Tick the PDF against the posting in AFAS.
Correct the break or send the document back to the buyer or the site.
drudgery: Recalculating totals the ledger has already computed.
Opening every invoice to confirm a code that has been the same for a year.
Ticking supplier statements line by line where the reference already matches.
today.time_sinks: The check is repeated on invoices that match exactly, because the queue shows every document and the breaks.

lenses.faster: The line-by-line recalculation and the tick on clean invoices disappear. The bookkeeper reviews a break list, and that review is about a third of the time this check takes now.
lenses.autonomous: Every proposed or posted line starts the tests for total, VAT code, duplicate invoice number and the supplier's default account. Clean lines pass, and only the breaks reach the bookkeeper.
lenses.ambitious: Hand the night-shift team leaders a morning list of receipts they entered after the office closed, named by load, which today surfaces only when a supplier chases. Demand would grow if the list were cheap, because peak season pushes more receipts onto the night shift at all three sites.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss ticking invoices that already add up. People want the real breaks: a VAT number that changed, a near-duplicate amount, or warehouse cost sitting on an office account.
lenses.options: Showing the same carrier invoice under Dutch 21% VAT and under reverse charge changes whether it is accepted or sent back. The total can be right under both treatments, so the draft is the decision.
lenses.altitude: The week is the break list and the supplier statements that do not tie. They gain the right to block a posting that fails the VAT or duplicate test before it can be paid, and the job becomes more expert because the easy ticks leave the day.
reach: The Accountant's check that the creditors and debtors sub-ledgers tie to the trial balance for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, once they learn which items the Controller treats as a reconciling item and which as a posting error.

tasks.human_edge: A figure can add up and still be the wrong document: a second invoice for the same container, a credit that belongs in last period, or a VAT code that is valid and wrong for intra-EU transport. The bookkeeper has the shipment; the test has the numbers.
tasks.pattern_why: Totals, VAT percentage, duplicate invoice number and the supplier's default account are pass-or-fail tests. AFAS can run them without a model, and a person sees only the fails.

in_practice.trigger: A line is proposed or posted in AFAS, or a supplier statement is imported.
steps: AFAS recalculates totals and VAT and compares them with the document.
It flags a duplicate invoice number, a VAT code outside the supplier's default, and an account the supplier has not used before.
Clean lines stay posted.
The bookkeeper opens the break list, corrects the code, or sends the document back.
The result of each break is written on the posting.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper clears every break before the invoice can go into a payment run. Clean lines pass without a second tick.
data_needed: Supplier default ledger account and VAT code
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS posting, with the test that failed, the old value, the new value and the user who cleared it.

evidence.claim: AFAS matches bank lines on payment reference, IBAN and invoice number, then on sums, and sends the misses to a person. Exact amounts apply unless a tolerance is set.
Touchless invoice processing disappoints where each administration keeps its own ledger accounts, VAT codes and exceptions.
Coding suggested from vendor history is meant to be reviewed and confirmed, so accountability stays with a person.

risks: A tolerance that is a bit wide will pass a real difference and take it off the break list.
A total-check will pass an intra-EU transport invoice booked with the wrong VAT treatment.
Once clean items are skipped, a bad VAT default can run for months before anyone sees it.
Agency invoices that fail the check can still name a worker. The break note should keep that name out of mail to the site.
research_questions: How many posted invoices a week fail a total, duplicate or VAT-code test, and who finds them today?
What amount tolerance is set in AFAS, and who agreed it?
Which VAT codes differ between domestic transport, intra-EU transport and warehouse services?
Do the three agencies' invoices show wage tax and VAT as separate amounts that a rule can read?

tasks.short: Put the right account, VAT code and site on each invoice

today.trigger: An invoice or credit note is in AFAS without a complete account, VAT code or site.
steps: Read the line description and pick the ledger account from the coding guide.
Choose the VAT code and the site or cost centre.
Split a mixed invoice across warehouse and office, or across the three sites.
Post the coding, or park it until the buyer or the site confirms.
drudgery: Looking up the same supplier's account for the hundredth time.
Copying last month's coding onto this month's bill.
Splitting an agency invoice across sites in Excel after the PDF has already been posted to one account.
today.time_sinks: Suppliers that describe the same work differently every month, and agency invoices that mix hours for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.

lenses.faster: For a supplier whose last invoices all use one account, the suggestion is on screen and the bookkeeper confirms it. New suppliers, mixed sites and agency bills still take the coding conversation they take today, so about three fifths of the task remains.
lenses.autonomous: When a UBL file or a scanned PDF creates a proposal, a suggested account, VAT code and site are attached from the text and from that supplier's history. The proposal waits until the bookkeeper confirms or changes it.
lenses.ambitious: Split each staffing-agency invoice across the three sites from the hours on the agency portal, and separate the g-rekening share, as a weekly file for the Controller and for Payroll. They do not get that file today. Demand would grow if it were cheap, because flex headcount rises toward 300 in peak season and FP&A currently forecasts that cost as one lump.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss hunting the coding guide for a supplier they already know. People want the mixed bills: three sites on one agency invoice, fuel and freight on one carrier bill, a credit note that does not name the load.
lenses.options: Three coding drafts for a mixed carrier invoice, all freight, freight plus fuel on a separate account, or a split by site, change warehouse cost and the forecast. One suggestion hides the choice.
lenses.altitude: Known suppliers take a confirmation. The week shifts to mixed and new invoices, and they gain the right to accept a suggestion only where that supplier's history is one account, and to send anything new back to the buyer or the site. The job becomes more expert on those exceptions.
reach: The FP&A analyst's first coding of unbilled freight accruals, once they learn how the forecast treats cost that has been receipted and not yet invoiced, and which period the Controller assigns it to.

tasks.human_edge: The written coding guide does not settle a fuel surcharge, a Venlo cross-dock that must stay in Venlo, or an agency hour that is warehouse work under the warehouse CAO rather than driving under the transport CAO. The bookkeeper and the buyer know the shipment.
tasks.pattern_why: A supplier with one stable account is a table lookup. The lines that still take the time are free-text descriptions, mixed sites and agency bills, and one model call can turn that text into a suggested account, VAT code and site for the bookkeeper to confirm. A proposal is not a posting.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS has a new invoice whose account, VAT code or site is empty.
steps: The invoice text and the supplier's posted history are passed to a single coding step.
That step returns a proposed ledger account, VAT code and site, plus the history line it leaned on.
Where the supplier's last invoices all share one account, the proposal is marked as history.
The bookkeeper confirms or edits every proposal.
Confirmed lines post. Mixed agency invoices stay parked until the portal hours are attached.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper confirms or changes the account, VAT code and site on every invoice before it posts. Nothing posts from the suggestion alone.
data_needed: Chart of accounts and VAT codes
Agency hours by site, when the supplier is an agency
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS invoice, with the proposed code, the code that was posted, and the user who confirmed it.

evidence.claim: Coding can be suggested from vendor history for the team to review and confirm. The same case says routine invoices process themselves.
Calling a booking proposal 'automation' overstates it. Own ledger accounts, VAT codes and exceptions per administration are why touchless shares disappoint, and PDFs keep arriving.
Where a PDF has no UBL, AFAS fills what it can from KvK, VAT number and IBAN, and a person fills the gaps.

Noordhaven can be held liable for an agency's unpaid wage tax and VAT. A payment-behaviour statement, proper records and payment of that part into the agency's g-rekening are the controls the tax authority describes.

risks: A confident suggestion on the wrong account gets confirmed in bulk because the pile is large, and last year's coding mistakes get repeated.
Agency cost coded to one site makes the other sites' results wrong and can miss the g-rekening split, which is the inlenersaansprakelijkheid exposure.

Invoice lines from agencies can contain worker names. Those names do not belong in the ledger text or in a mail to the site, and a check that starts ranking named flex workers is a works-council matter.
This step reads invoices, not people. Using the same flow to score a supplier or a worker would be a different system and needs its own check under the EU AI Act.
research_questions: For how many suppliers is the ledger account the same on the last ten invoices?
What share of suggested lines does a bookkeeper change, counted over four weeks?
Do the three agency portals export hours by site and week in a file AFAS or Excel can read?
Who may add a ledger account or a VAT code, and is that list short enough to keep up to date?

tasks.short: Work out what is due, including discount and interest

today.trigger: A customer or a supplier asks for a balance, a discount is claimed, or interest comes up on a late trade invoice.
steps: Pull the open items from AFAS, or from an Excel copy of them.
Apply the discount days or the interest days by hand.
Check the result against the invoice and the contract terms.
Send the figure or book the settlement.
drudgery: Rebuilding a balance that the open items already hold.
Counting days in Excel for a discount the payment terms already state.
Redoing the same sum after each partial payment until the open item is clean.
today.time_sinks: Short-pays and partial payments, where the arithmetic is repeated until someone decides what the remainder is.

lenses.faster: The balance, the discount and the interest calculate from the open item and the terms. What stays is the short-pay and the discount claimed after the window, about a fifth of the time this task takes now.
lenses.autonomous: A posting, a customer receipt or a due date starts the calculation, and AFAS updates the open amount and the discount window. The bookkeeper steps in when a payment is short, a discount is late, or interest is actually going to be billed.
lenses.ambitious: Each Monday, give the Credit and Collections Officer the debtors still inside a discount window and the ones that have crossed the date interest is allowed. The officer now looks at that only when a large debtor is already late. If the list were cheap, the officer would use it on mid-sized shippers too, so demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss counting days and rekeying totals. People want the short-pay conversation: a damaged load, a wrong rate, or a discount that is no longer fair.
lenses.options: For a short-paid freight invoice the bookkeeper can set out three settlements: take the discount, refuse it, or release the undisputed part and park the rest. Those drafts change the cash and the open item, so the choice is the decision.
lenses.altitude: Arithmetic leaves the week, which moves to short-pays and to terms that do not match the contract. They gain the right to refuse a discount claimed after the window and to flag a term longer than 30 days on a small supplier before the payment run. The job becomes more expert.
reach: The Credit and Collections Officer's aging pack, the part that is balances and dates, once they learn which disputes the officer owns and which payment promises are already agreed. The call to the customer stays with the officer.

tasks.human_edge: Granting a discount a day late to a shipper who had a truck waiting at Venlo, or charging interest to a customer who is also a large outbound account, is a commercial call. The amount can be calculated. The waiver sits with the officer and with the bookkeeper's knowledge of the file.
tasks.pattern_why: Amount due, settlement discount, open balance and interest are formulas on dates and terms. AFAS and a checked sheet calculate them. A model adds nothing to a 30-day term or a discount window.

in_practice.trigger: An open item is posted, a receipt is matched, or someone asks for a balance, a discount or interest.
steps: AFAS computes the open amount from the invoice, the payments and the credit notes.
It applies the discount only while the receipt date sits inside the term on the master.
It computes interest days from the due date when the contract says interest is due.
Short-pays, late discount claims and any interest that would actually be invoiced land on a list.
The bookkeeper checks that list and books the settlement they agree with the Credit and Collections Officer.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper approves any settlement that waives a discount, writes off a short-pay, or charges interest. Plain open-item balances update on their own.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS open item, with the formula inputs, the settlement chosen and the user who approved a waiver.

evidence.claim: As a large company, Noordhaven may not agree a payment term longer than 30 days with a small supplier.
Open-item balances, settlement discount and interest follow from dates and terms once those sit on the ledger. That arithmetic does not need a model.

risks: Interest or discount counted from the wrong date, such as invoice date where the contract uses the receipt date.
A term over 30 days with a small supplier stays invisible when the supplier master has no small-supplier flag.
An Excel copy of the open items drifts away from AFAS and the figure in the mail is the old one.
A waiver agreed in Teams and never written on the open item will resurface as a dispute next month.
research_questions: Which discount and interest rules are in AFAS payment terms, and which live only in Excel or in a contract PDF?
How many open items a month are short-paid or paid inside a discount window?
Does the supplier master mark small suppliers, so a term over 30 days can be flagged?
Who may waive interest or a missed discount: the bookkeeper, or the Credit and Collections Officer?

tasks.short: Build the payment run for suppliers, tax and the utilities

today.trigger: It is payment-run day, or a utility bill, a tax assessment or an agency invoice has reached its due date.
steps: Select the due, approved invoices in AFAS, including utilities and tax.
Recalculate the batch total and the g-rekening part of each agency invoice.
Create the payment file for Rabobank and check the IBANs against the supplier master.
Release the batch under the company's payment rule.
Match the bank line when the CAMT.053 file comes back.
drudgery: Retyping IBANs and invoice references into the bank file.
Splitting the wage-tax and VAT part of an agency invoice by hand.
Checking the same utility amount, on the same reference, every month.
today.time_sinks: Invoices that are approved late, and IBAN changes that have to be confirmed with the supplier before anyone will release the payment.

lenses.faster: Building the file from approved, due invoices disappears, including the ordinary utility and tax lines. Release, IBAN warnings and agency invoices that do not match the hours remain, about half the time this task takes now.
lenses.autonomous: The payment calendar starts the run. AFAS builds a batch from invoices that are approved and due, splits the g-rekening share on agency invoices, and holds the file. Rabobank receives it only after the bookkeeper approves that batch.
lenses.ambitious: Put small carriers on a fixed weekly run that pays them inside 30 days, a service they miss when the invoice waits in an email approval. Demand would grow if adding a carrier to that run were cheap, because the long tail of small suppliers is who waits today.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss assembling the file and retyping payment references. People want the odd payment: a changed IBAN, a duplicate that looks new, an agency bill that does not match the hours, a tax assessment that is not the usual VAT amount.
lenses.options: Two batch drafts, one that pays a disputed carrier now and one that holds that invoice until the site confirms the load, change the cash leaving Rabobank and whether the 30-day clock is met. One combined batch hides that choice.
lenses.altitude: File building leaves the day. The week is release, held invoices and supplier-master fixes, and they gain the right to hold one invoice out of an otherwise clean batch and to refuse an IBAN change that has not been confirmed. The job becomes more expert on fraud and on agency liability.
reach: The Controller's 14-day list of what will leave the Rabobank account, once they learn which wage-tax and payroll amounts the Controller adds outside the creditors ledger. The Finance Director's release limit stays where it is.

tasks.human_edge: After an IBAN-name warning, the bank still sends the payment if the payer confirms it. Deciding that a new IBAN really is the supplier, and that the g-rekening share on an agency invoice is the right amount, takes a person who can check the payment-behaviour statement or call the supplier.
tasks.pattern_why: The batch is a rule: due date, approved invoice, IBAN on the master, duplicate check, and the g-rekening share for the three agencies. Paper cheques are rare here, so the output is a Rabobank batch with a person releasing it. A model is not required to build that file.

in_practice.trigger: The payment calendar opens the run, or a utility, tax or agency invoice reaches its due date.
steps: AFAS selects invoices that are posted, approved and due, and drops anything blocked or already paid.
It calculates the g-rekening part for the three agencies and the remainder to the ordinary IBAN.
It raises IBAN changes, duplicate invoice numbers and amounts that differ from the posted invoice.
The bookkeeper reviews the batch, holds the warned lines, and releases the rest to Rabobank.
When the CAMT.053 file returns, AFAS matches the paid lines and parks the rest.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper approves each Rabobank batch before it is sent, and holds any line with an IBAN-name warning, a duplicate, or an agency split that does not match the invoice.
data_needed: Approved open invoices and due dates
Agency g-rekening IBAN and the wage-tax and VAT share
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS payment run, with the user who released it, the lines held back, and the reason for each hold.

evidence.claim: Since October 2025, Dutch banks check the payee name against the IBAN. A payer who confirms the payment after a warning is not blocked by the bank.
A hirer can be liable for a staffing agency's unpaid wage tax and VAT, and limits that by records, a payment-behaviour statement, and by paying that part into the agency's g-rekening.
A large company may not agree a payment term of more than 30 days with a small supplier.
In a Wolters Kluwer survey of 594 respondents, 70% still approve invoices on paper or by email, and 43% say this regularly delays payment.

risks: Confirming an IBAN-name warning clears the bank's check and the money still leaves. A rushed release after the warning is the fraud path.
Paying an agency in full to the ordinary account, and missing the g-rekening, leaves the inlenersaansprakelijkheid exposure in place.
The same utility or carrier invoice arriving as both PDF and UBL can be paid twice if the duplicate test only looks at one of the two numbers.
A term agreed past 30 days with a small supplier, or an approval that sits in email, makes the weekly run late even when the file itself is quick. Paper cheques are not the control that catches this.
research_questions: Who releases a batch today, one bookkeeper, a second person, or the Controller above a threshold?
What share of payments to the three agencies went to a g-rekening last quarter, and against which payment-behaviour statement?
How many Rabobank IBAN-name warnings appeared in the last three months, and how many were confirmed?
How many small-supplier invoices were paid after day 30, and was the cause the term on the master or a late approval?

tasks.short: See whether AFAS, the bank and the side sheets agree

today.trigger: The CAMT.053 file arrives, an agency portal total is checked, or a site's Excel sheet is compared with AFAS during the month or at close.
steps: Export the AFAS journal, open items or bank lines.
Set them beside the Excel sheet, the agency portal or the bank list.
Tick line by line on amount and reference.
Note the breaks and correct them, or explain them for the close file.
drudgery: Ticking lines that already match on amount and reference.
Keeping an Excel journal that repeats what AFAS holds.
Reconciling a portal total that uses a different week or a different site name.
today.time_sinks: Breaks that are only timing, and references that differ by a prefix, so the same payment is hunted twice.

lenses.faster: Bank lines and portal totals that equal a posted invoice drop off the list. The bookkeeper works the unmatched lines and the Excel sheets that have no invoice number, about two fifths of the time this compare takes now.
lenses.autonomous: Arrival of the CAMT.053 file or a saved portal export starts the match. Hits on reference, IBAN, invoice number or an exact sum clear themselves. Lines with no key, or present in only one system, wait for the bookkeeper.
lenses.ambitious: Tie flex hours from the three agency portals to the agency invoice during the week, for night-shift hours as well as day-shift hours, and give the difference to Payroll and the site manager while the week is still open. Night shift is not covered by today's daytime tick. Demand would grow in peak season, when flex headcount moves toward 300 and a missed difference costs more.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss ticking a printout. People want a real break: a bank line with no invoice, a portal hour total above the bill, or a site sheet that does not use AFAS invoice numbers.
lenses.options: An unmatched customer receipt can be drafted as a short-pay against one invoice or as cash on account. The two drafts change the aging and the cash forecast, and the bookkeeper picks the one the remittance advice supports.
lenses.altitude: The week is unmatched items, and Excel side books that duplicate AFAS get retired as each one gains a reference. They gain the right to refuse a supplier or agency file that has no invoice number or payment reference, and the job becomes more expert on the breaks that move the close.
reach: The Accountant's bank reconciliation up to the explained differences, once they learn the close timetable and which differences the Controller wants left open. The Accountant still signs the trial balance.

tasks.human_edge: A round-number difference can be a missing credit, a bank charge, or a payment that belongs to another administration. The bookkeeper recognises the pattern from earlier months. A match rule can only mark the line as open.
tasks.pattern_why: AFAS already matches CAMT.053 lines on reference, IBAN and invoice number, then on sums, and parks the rest. Comparing a portal total or an Excel sheet that carries the same key is the same kind of rule. A written explanation of a failed line can come later.

in_practice.trigger: A CAMT.053 file arrives from Rabobank, or a portal export or Excel sheet is dropped in for the week.
steps: AFAS matches bank lines on payment reference, IBAN and invoice number, then on exact sums.
Portal hours and Excel lines that carry an invoice number or a week-and-site key are compared with the posted invoices.
Exact hits clear.
Lines outside the key, or outside any agreed tolerance, stay on the break list.
The bookkeeper explains or corrects each break and files the reason on the reconciliation.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper signs off the break list. Matched lines clear without a tick. A tolerance above zero is applied only where Finance has already agreed the amount.
data_needed: AFAS open items and journal lines
Agency portal export with site and week
Excel side sheets, where they carry a reference
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS bank-match log and the reconciliation note, with the key used and the user who explained each open line.

evidence.claim: AFAS matches CAMT.053 lines on payment reference, IBAN and invoice number, then oldest-first on sums. Amounts must be exact unless a tolerance is set, and misses go to a person.
PDFs and receipts keep arriving, which is one reason a fully touchless process still leaves a queue for a person.
Paper journals and cheques are not the main side record in a company on AFAS, Rabobank batches and agency portals. The side records to tie are the bank file, the portals and Excel.

risks: A sum-match can clear two different invoices that happen to add up to the payment, and hide both errors.
An Excel sheet that is edited after the compare leaves the close file looking tied when the sheet no longer is.
Agency hours with no site can tie to the invoice total and still put all the cost on the wrong warehouse.
A tie that uses named flex workers to chase productivity, rather than to check an invoice, is a works-council matter and an AVG one. The compare should stop at hours, site and amount.
research_questions: Which journals are still kept in Excel, and which of them have an invoice number or payment reference on every line?
What percentage of CAMT.053 lines auto-match in AFAS today, and what are the top reasons for the rest?
Do the three agency portals export hours with a site, a week and an identifier that can be tied to an invoice without putting a worker's name on the reconciliation?
What amount tolerance is set, and has a sum-match ever cleared the wrong combination of invoices?

tasks.short: Look up an account and answer the question

today.trigger: A supplier, a customer, a site manager or FP&A asks by Outlook or by Teams about an invoice, a payment or a balance.
steps: Read the question and find the invoice number, supplier or debtor.
Look up status, amount and date in AFAS.
Check Outlook or the receipt when the posting does not explain the question.
Write the reply and attach a statement when one is asked for.
drudgery: Answering the same 'has this been paid' question several times a day.
Copying open items into a mail by hand.
Hunting a load or a week number because the question never gives an invoice number.
today.time_sinks: Questions that name a shipment and no invoice, and questions that wait because the bookkeeper is still in the posting queue.

lenses.faster: Finding the open item and drafting a status reply disappear for questions that name an invoice, a supplier or a debtor. The bookkeeper still reads and sends, and questions with no document number take almost as long as today, so a bit over half the task remains.
lenses.autonomous: A mail or a Teams question that names an invoice, a supplier or a debtor starts a lookup and a draft. The draft quotes the AFAS fields it used. It is sent only after the bookkeeper approves it.
lenses.ambitious: Answer the three site planning desks, including questions the night shift leaves overnight, with a morning note of what was paid and what is blocked. Those desks wait today until a bookkeeper is in. Demand would grow if the note were cheap, because the desks already work around the wait by phoning.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss typing 'paid last Thursday, reference as follows' for the fifth time. People want the question that is really a missing receipt or a dispute, where the answer changes what gets paid.
lenses.options: Two drafts to a supplier who says they were not paid, one that it was paid and here is the bank reference, and one that it is open because the receipt match failed, lead to different next steps. Sending the wrong draft creates a second dispute.
lenses.altitude: Less of the week goes to status mail, and more goes to disputes and missing documents. They gain the right to release a plain status reply that only quotes AFAS, while any reply that admits a short-pay, a delay or a promise of payment still waits for them. The job becomes more expert on the disputes.
reach: The Credit and Collections Officer's factual replies on whether a credit note is posted, once they learn which debtors the officer has promised to call in person. The collection call stays with the officer.

tasks.human_edge: The bookkeeper can tell a payment chase from a complaint, and can hear that a site manager is really asking for a cost to move before the close. A draft that only quotes the open item will answer a question the sender did not ask. Anything that states a legal position stays with the person.
tasks.pattern_why: The incoming message mixes status, a missing document and a dispute in an order the bookkeeper cannot know in advance, so the lookup path is not one fixed query. The draft still has to be built from AFAS fields, and the bookkeeper approves it before it counts as sent.

in_practice.trigger: An Outlook or Teams message asks about an invoice, a supplier, a debtor or a payment.
steps: The message is read for invoice number, party, amount and site.
AFAS is queried for the open item, the payment date and the match status.
If the message is a plain status question, a reply is drafted that quotes those fields and the source line.
If the message is a dispute, a missing receipt or a promise to pay, the draft is marked for the bookkeeper to rewrite.
The bookkeeper sends, edits or drops the draft. The unsent draft expires.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper approves every outgoing reply. A status draft can be sent in a batch. A draft that admits a short-pay, a delay or a date of payment is rewritten first.
data_needed: AFAS open item, payment status and match result
Invoice number, supplier or debtor, and site
in_practice.logs_to: The sent mail or Teams reply, stored with the AFAS lines it quoted and the user who approved it.

evidence.claim: Once AFAS has posted a matched invoice, the payment status sits on that posting and can be read back for a reply.
Unmatched bank lines stay with a person, so a status answer given before the match can say an invoice is open when the cash is already on the account.
Many Dutch companies still handle invoice approval by paper or email, so suppliers keep asking where a payment stands. In one survey, 70% approve that way.
A reply that leaves the company should stay tied to the ledger figures, and the figures used should be kept with the reply.

risks: A draft that says an invoice will be paid on a date the payment run has not released.
Worker names or pay details from an agency invoice copied into a reply that goes wider than the person who asked, which is an AVG problem.
A dispute treated as a status question and closed by the draft.
A sentence in the draft that does not match the AFAS line it claims to quote. The approver has to see the source line, not only the sentence.
research_questions: How many account and payment questions arrive per week by mail and by Teams, and how many are a straight status?
Which questions may be answered from AFAS fields alone, and which must be rewritten every time?
Do these messages contain worker names or agency pay data that must not be repeated in the reply?
Over two weeks, what share of drafts would a bookkeeper send without editing the figures?

tasks.short: Keep an eye on who is late to pay or to be paid

today.trigger: The bookkeeper looks through overdue debtors, supplier due dates, and any lease schedule kept beside the ledger.
steps: Export the aging from AFAS or rebuild it in Excel.
Mark debtors who are late and suppliers Noordhaven is about to pay late.
Tell the Credit and Collections Officer, or the supplier, which items are open.
Update the sheet so the same item is not chased twice.
drudgery: Rebuilding the aging in Excel from an export.
Scanning debtors and suppliers that are still inside their terms.
Chasing an item whose cash is already on the bank statement and not yet matched.
today.time_sinks: Accounts that flip between current and overdue because a receipt is unmatched, and the nightly Power BI extract that is already a day behind the question.

lenses.faster: The pass over accounts that are inside terms disappears. The bookkeeper works the overdue debtors and the supplier invoices about to breach their due date, about a third of the time this watch takes now.
lenses.autonomous: A morning job on the AFAS open items starts it. Accounts inside terms stay quiet. Overdue debtors, and supplier invoices close to their due date, land on a list. The list does not contact the customer.
lenses.ambitious: Give the two FP&A analysts a twice-weekly view of which debtors will miss the cash forecast, a view they now rebuild by hand around month-end from the nightly extract. If it were cheap they would use it in ordinary weeks as well, so demand would grow, and the decision to reforecast cash would be made far more often than at close.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss scrolling the accounts that are inside terms. People want the few that are late for a reason the aging does not show: a rate dispute, a damaged load, a debtor who pays on statement.
lenses.options: Two cash pictures for the large debtors, one where the promised receipts arrive this week and one where they slip a month, change whether FP&A revises the forecast the business is asked to trust. A single overdue total leaves that call unmade.
lenses.altitude: The daily scan becomes a short list. They gain the right to place a debtor on the collections list and to pull a small supplier forward in the payment run so the company stays inside 30 days. The job becomes more expert on which late account matters, and the customer call stays with the Credit and Collections Officer.
reach: The FP&A analyst's mechanical update of cash in and days sales outstanding from the open items, once they learn how the forecast separates 'expected this week' from 'overdue but promised'. The forecast commentary stays with FP&A.

tasks.human_edge: A late shipper may be disputing a damage claim at Venlo, and a small supplier may be hurt by day 35 in a way a large carrier is not. The aging has the date. The bookkeeper has the file, and the Credit and Collections Officer has the relationship.
tasks.pattern_why: Overdue trade accounts and invoices approaching their due date are a selection on open items, due dates and unmatched cash. AFAS can produce that list each morning. The chase and any waiver stay with a person.

in_practice.trigger: Each morning after the bank match, and again before a payment run.
steps: AFAS lists debtors past their due date and suppliers due inside the next five days.
It separates items whose cash is already on an unmatched bank line.
It flags small suppliers whose open invoices would pass 30 days.
The bookkeeper reviews the list, moves clean small-supplier invoices into the payment run, and passes disputed debtors to the Credit and Collections Officer.
FP&A receives the twice-weekly cash picture from the same list.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper decides which debtors go to the Credit and Collections Officer and which supplier invoices are pulled forward. The list itself sends nothing to a customer or a supplier.
data_needed: Promises already logged by the Credit and Collections Officer
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS open item, with the date it was flagged, the action taken, and the user who took it.

evidence.claim: A large company may not agree more than 30 days with a small supplier, so supplier due dates are a compliance watch as well as a cash watch.
AFAS leaves unmatched bank lines with a person, so an aging run before that match overstates what is overdue.
An open-item ledger can list trade debtors and trade creditors by due date. Days sales outstanding at Noordhaven is fed from that list, not from a separate loan system.

risks: Chasing a debtor whose cash is already at Rabobank and still unmatched.
Missing a 30-day breach on a small supplier because the master has no size flag.
Treating an equipment-lease instalment like a trade invoice and missing a final payment that sits outside the aging.
Mailing customers from this list would cut across the Credit and Collections Officer, and mailing a named flex worker about pay would pull the task into HR data the bookkeeper should not run.
research_questions: Is there a loan or lease book in AFAS, or is this watch entirely trade debtors, trade creditors and the tax calendar?
Over one month, how often is the aging wrong because cash is unmatched?
Does FP&A use a list from the bookkeeper today, or rebuild cash from the nightly Power BI extract?
Which supplier records identify a small supplier for the 30-day test?

role.altitude: The three bookkeepers move from keying invoices and ticking lists to a short queue of breaks: bad files, mixed agency bills, unmatched cash and payments that need a hold. They gain the right to set match tolerances, send a bad supplier file back, hold one invoice out of a Rabobank batch, refuse an unconfirmed IBAN, and flag a small-supplier term past 30 days. The job becomes more expert. Days to close shrink only if the untouched invoices are already posted before close week.
reach: The Accountant's sub-ledger tie-out and the explained bank reconciliation, up to the point where the Accountant signs the trial balance.
The Credit and Collections Officer's aging pack and factual 'is it posted' replies. The collection call and any commercial waiver stay with the officer.
The FP&A analyst's mechanical cash-in and days-sales-outstanding update from open items. The forecast narrative stays with FP&A.
The Controller's prepared file for the g-rekening split and the inlenersaansprakelijkheid check on the three agencies. The sign-off stays with the Controller.
Payroll's difference list between agency hours and the agency invoice. The payroll run itself stays with the Payroll Specialist.
role.ceiling_note: The ceiling is judgment, dual control and the documents that still arrive as PDF, not keying speed. Recording is about 103 hours a year per FTE and can shrink; close week, peak-season flex (up to 300 workers) and supplier disputes set the floor. Three people cannot also become the Controller or the credit function. This role does not take the absence file under the Wet verbetering poortwachter. The works council has a say if a match on agency hours starts following named flex workers. Under the EU AI Act this stays a low-stakes document and ledger process only while it does not score workers or make a credit decision about a person.
skills_to_grow: Match rules, tolerances and VAT codes in AFAS, including reverse charge and intra-EU transport.
The g-rekening split and the payment-behaviour statement for the three staffing agencies.
IBAN-name warnings and how a supplier-master change is confirmed.
Reading a CAMT.053 break and a small-supplier invoice heading past 30 days.
Enough of the close and the cash forecast to hand FP&A a difference that is already explained.
role.ambitious_version: The bookkeeper runs the exception desk for procure-to-pay and order-to-cash across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, including the night shift's receipts. Agency cost is split by site in the week it is worked, small carriers are paid inside 30 days, and FP&A gets a cash list before the nightly dashboard. The month closes faster because the invoices that match are already posted, and the adjustments that remain are named. The role stays, because someone still has to decide the breaks the forecast depends on.
